chapterTitle: The Thousand Years and the Great White Throne
themeTitle: “Blessed and Holy Is He Who Has Part in the First Resurrection”

scripture.text: I saw an angel coming down out of heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, “I saw an angel coming down out of heaven” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). After the beast and false prophet (19:20), now the dragon. ἔχοντα τὴν κλεῖν τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ ἅλυσιν μεγάλην ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ, “having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand” — κλείς; ἅλυσις, a manacle. Not even a mighty archangel is needed: an ordinary angel binds the devil. Christ holds the keys (1:18); His servant uses them.

scripture.text: He seized the dragon, the old serpent, which is the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole inhabited earth, and bound him for a thousand years,
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐκράτησεν τὸν δράκοντα, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὅς ἐστιν Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, “He seized the dragon, the old serpent, which is the devil and Satan” — κρατέω, from the hold family: to grip and overpower. The same four names as 12:9. ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην is added in some manuscripts, “who deceives the whole inhabited earth” — οἰκουμένη, from the world family. καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν χίλια ἔτη, “and bound him for a thousand years” — δέω, to bind; ἔτος, from the time family: a year, as distinct from χρόνος, a span, and καιρός, a season. ‘A thousand years’ appears six times in verses 2–7.

scripture.text: and cast him into the abyss, and shut it, and sealed it over him, that he should deceive the nations no more, until the thousand years were finished. After this, he must be freed for a short time.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον καὶ ἔκλεισεν καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, “and cast him into the abyss, and shut it, and sealed it over him” — three verbs: thrown, locked, sealed. ἵνα μὴ πλανήσῃ ἔτι τὰ ἔθνη, “that he should deceive the nations no more” — the purpose is specific: his power to deceive the nations is stopped. ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη, “until the thousand years were finished” — τελέω, from the perfect family; ἔτος, from the time family. μετὰ ταῦτα δεῖ λυθῆναι αὐτὸν μικρὸν χρόνον, “After this, he must be freed for a short time” — δεῖ, God's necessity; χρόνος, from the time family: a brief span.

scripture.text: I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them. I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of God, and such as didn’t worship the beast nor his image, and didn’t receive the mark on their forehead and on their hand. They lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον θρόνους, καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐπ᾽ αὐτούς, καὶ κρίμα ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς, “I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); κρίμα, from the judge family: the verdict is given in their favour, and authority to judge is given to them (Daniel 7:22). καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν πεπελεκισμένων διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, “I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of God” — ψυχή, from the life family; πελεκίζω, beheaded with an axe; μαρτυρία, from the witness family; λόγος, from the word family. καὶ οἵτινες οὐ προσεκύνησαν τὸ θηρίον οὐδὲ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, “and such as didn’t worship the beast nor his image” — εἰκών, from the image family. καὶ ἔζησαν καὶ ἐβασίλευσαν μετὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ χίλια ἔτη, “They lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years” — ζάω, from the life family; ἔτος, from the time family. Those the beast ‘overcame’ (13:7) reign.

scripture.text: The rest of the dead didn’t live until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.
scripture.understanding: οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔζησαν ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη, “The rest of the dead didn’t live until the thousand years were finished” — ζάω, from the life family; τελέω, from the perfect family; ἔτος, from the time family. αὕτη ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη, “This is the first resurrection” — ἀνάστασις, from the rise family: a standing up again. Some take it as a bodily resurrection of believers at Christ's return, before the thousand years; others as the new life believers receive when they die and go to reign with Christ (or are spiritually raised with Him now, Ephesians 2:6), with the bodily resurrection of all at the end.

scripture.text: Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection. Over these, the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him one thousand years.
scripture.understanding: μακάριος καὶ ἅγιος ὁ ἔχων μέρος ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ πρώτῃ, “Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection” — the fifth blessing; ἅγιος, from the holy family; ἀνάστασις, from the rise family. ἐπὶ τούτων ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν, “Over these, the second death has no power” — ἐξουσία, from the power family: the second death (v. 14) has no authority over them (2:11). ἀλλ᾽ ἔσονται ἱερεῖς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ χίλια ἔτη, “but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him one thousand years” — ἔτος, from the time family. The promise of 1:6 and 5:10 fulfilled: a kingdom of priests.

scripture.text: And after the thousand years, Satan will be released from his prison,
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ὅταν τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη, “And after the thousand years” — τελέω, from the perfect family; ἔτος, from the time family. λυθήσεται ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς αὐτοῦ, “Satan will be released from his prison” — λύω; φυλακή. Why release him? Perhaps to show that even after a long reign of righteousness, the human heart apart from grace is still ready to rebel, and that God's final judgement is entirely just.

scripture.text: and he will come out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to the war; the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐξελεύσεται πλανῆσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὰ ἐν ταῖς τέσσαρσι γωνίαις τῆς γῆς, “and he will come out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. τὸν Γὼγ καὶ Μαγώγ, “Gog and Magog” — in Ezekiel 38–39 Gog of the land of Magog leads the nations against God's people and is destroyed. Here they stand for all the nations in final rebellion. συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον, ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, “to gather them together to the war; the number of whom is as the sand of the sea” — the same gathering ‘for the war’ as 16:14 and 19:19. Many see these as three views of one final battle.

scripture.text: They went up over the width of the earth, and surrounded the camp of the saints, and the beloved city. Fire came down out of heaven from God and devoured them.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἀνέβησαν ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς, “They went up over the width of the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. καὶ ἐκύκλευσαν τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἠγαπημένην, “and surrounded the camp of the saints, and the beloved city” — παρεμβολή, a camp: God's people are still pilgrims; ἅγιος, from the holy family; ἀγαπάω, from the love family: the city God loves — His people. καὶ κατέβη πῦρ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτούς, “Fire came down out of heaven from God and devoured them” — as on Gog in Ezekiel 38:22, and on Elijah's enemies. No battle; God simply ends it.

scripture.text: The devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet are also. They will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ διάβολος ὁ πλανῶν αὐτοὺς ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ θείου, “The devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur” — διάβολος; λίμνη. The deceiver's career ends. ὅπου καὶ τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, “where the beast and the false prophet are also” — the whole unholy trinity together (19:20). καὶ βασανισθήσονται ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, “They will be tormented day and night forever and ever” — ἡμέρα, from the time family; αἰών, from the time family and the world family. Satan's defeat is total and final.

scripture.text: I saw a great white throne, and him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away. There was found no place for them.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον θρόνον μέγαν λευκόν, “I saw a great white throne” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). Great in majesty; white in perfect purity and justice. καὶ τὸν καθήμενον ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν, “and him who sat on it” — God; and Jesus said the Father has given all judgement to the Son. οὗ ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου ἔφυγεν ἡ γῆ καὶ ὁ οὐρανός, καὶ τόπος οὐχ εὑρέθη αὐτοῖς, “from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away. There was found no place for them” — γῆ, from the world family. The old creation itself cannot stand before Him; there is nowhere to hide. Every person now stands before God alone.

scripture.text: I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works.
scripture.understanding: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς νεκρούς, τοὺς μεγάλους καὶ τοὺς μικρούς, ἑστῶτας ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, “I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). No one is too great to escape or too small to be overlooked. καὶ βιβλία ἠνοίχθησαν, “and they opened books” — βιβλίον, from the book family: the records of every life (Daniel 7:10). καὶ ἄλλο βιβλίον ἠνοίχθη, ὅ ἐστιν τῆς ζωῆς, “Another book was opened, which is the book of life” — ἄλλος, from the another family; ζωή, from the life family. καὶ ἐκρίθησαν οἱ νεκροὶ ἐκ τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τοῖς βιβλίοις κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν, “The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works” — κρίνω, from the judge family; ἔργον, from the work family. Two kinds of book: the record of works, and the book of grace.

scripture.text: The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them. They were judged, each one according to his works.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔδωκεν ἡ θάλασσα τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ, “The sea gave up the dead who were in it” — those lost without burial are not lost to God. καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἔδωκαν τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτοῖς, “Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them” — Christ holds their keys (1:18). καὶ ἐκρίθησαν ἕκαστος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν, “They were judged, each one according to his works” — κρίνω, from the judge family; ἔργον, from the work family: personally, individually, justly.

scripture.text: Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἐβλήθησαν εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός, “Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire” — the last enemy destroyed (1 Corinthians 15:26). Death itself dies. οὗτος ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερός ἐστιν, ἡ λίμνη τοῦ πυρός, “This is the second death, the lake of fire” — the first death separates body and soul; the second separates the person from God forever.

scripture.text: If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire.
scripture.understanding: καὶ εἴ τις οὐχ εὑρέθη ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ τῆς ζωῆς γεγραμμένος, “If anyone was not found written in the book of life” — βίβλος, from the book family: the register of citizens (3:5), as distinct from the βιβλία, the records of works (v. 12); ζωή, from the life family. ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός, “he was cast into the lake of fire” — no one is saved by the record of their works; only by having their name in the Lamb's book of life (13:8; 21:27).

visualMeditations.title: The Dragon Chained
visualMeditations.image: Picture the dragon who once swept stars from the sky and stood over the woman's child. Now an ordinary angel comes down, grabs him, wraps a great chain around him, throws him into the pit, slams it shut, locks it and seals it.
visualMeditations.meaning: “He seized the dragon, the old serpent, which is the devil and Satan... and bound him for a thousand years, and cast him into the abyss” (vv. 2–3). However terrifying the enemy seems, he is no match for God. He can be bound by a single angel.

visualMeditations.title: The Martyrs Enthroned
visualMeditations.image: Picture those who were beheaded in the arena for refusing the beast's image, their bodies thrown away in shame. Now see them seated on thrones, alive, reigning with Christ, priests of God, and the second death unable to touch them.
visualMeditations.meaning: “I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus... They lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years” (v. 4). “Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection” (v. 6). The world's verdict is reversed.

visualMeditations.title: The Great White Throne
visualMeditations.image: Picture heaven and earth fleeing away until nothing is left but a vast white throne and, before it, every human being who has ever lived — kings and beggars, famous and forgotten — standing alone. Books are opened. And one more book: the book of life.
visualMeditations.meaning: “I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life” (v. 12). Everyone will give account. The only safe place is to have your name in the Lamb's book.

visualMeditations.title: Death Thrown into the Fire
visualMeditations.image: Picture the sea, the grave and the realm of the dead giving up every person they held. Then picture Death and Hades themselves — the old enemies that have taken every generation — seized and hurled into the lake of fire.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire” (v. 14). The last enemy is destroyed. For those in Christ, death will never touch them again.

structure.label: Satan Bound (v. 1-3)
structure.body: An angel with the key of the abyss and a great chain seizes the dragon, binds him for a thousand years and seals him in the abyss so that he can no longer deceive the nations, until he is released for a short time.

structure.label: The Saints Reign (v. 4-6)
structure.body: John sees thrones given to those who judge, and the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and who refused the beast; they come to life and reign with Christ a thousand years; this is the first resurrection; blessed and holy are those who share in it, for the second death has no power over them.

structure.label: Satan's Final Rebellion and Defeat (v. 7-10)
structure.body: After the thousand years Satan is released and deceives the nations, Gog and Magog, gathering them against the camp of the saints and the beloved city; fire from heaven consumes them; the devil is thrown into the lake of fire with the beast and false prophet, to be tormented forever.

structure.label: The Great White Throne (v. 11-15)
structure.body: John sees a great white throne, from whose presence earth and heaven flee; the dead, great and small, stand before it; books are opened, including the book of life, and all are judged by their works; sea, Death and Hades give up their dead; Death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire, the second death, with anyone not found in the book of life.

sections.heading: The Thousand Years: How Christians Read It
paragraphs: Revelation 20 is the only passage in the Bible that speaks of a thousand-year reign, and Christians have read it in three main ways. Premillennialists believe Christ returns (ch. 19) before (‘pre’) a literal or long period of reign on earth, during which Satan is bound and resurrected believers reign with Christ; then comes Satan's final rebellion and the last judgement. Amillennialists believe the thousand years is a symbolic description of the present age between Christ's first and second comings: Satan was bound at the cross so that he can no longer prevent the gospel from reaching the nations, and believers who die reign with Christ in heaven. Postmillennialists believe the gospel will gradually transform the world into a long era of peace and righteousness before Christ returns.

Each reading has serious arguments. Premillennialists point out that chapter 20 follows Christ's return in chapter 19 and speaks of a resurrection in which people ‘lived’. Amillennialists point out that Revelation often goes back over the same period from different angles; that Jesus spoke of binding ‘the strong man’ in His ministry: “how can one enter into the house of the strong man, and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man?” (Matthew 12:29); that the binding is specifically so that Satan cannot ‘deceive the nations’ (v. 3); and that the gathering for war in verse 8 echoes 16:14 and 19:19, suggesting the same final battle.

Faithful, Bible-believing Christians hold each of these views, and this study will not pretend the question is settled. What all agree on is clear in the text: Satan's power is limited and his doom is certain; those who are faithful to Christ, even to death, will live and reign with Him; there will be a final judgement of all people; and death itself will be destroyed.

sections.heading: Satan Bound, the Saints Enthroned
paragraphs: An angel seizes “the dragon, the old serpent, which is the devil and Satan” and binds him for a thousand years, throwing him into the abyss “that he should deceive the nations no more, until the thousand years were finished” (vv. 2–3). The binding is specific: it stops him deceiving the nations. However one reads the timing, the picture is of Satan's power curbed by a single angel. The one who seemed so mighty in chapters 12–13 is helpless before God.

John then sees thrones, and “the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of God, and such as didn’t worship the beast nor his image... They lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years” (v. 4). Those whom the world condemned and executed now sit on thrones and share Christ's rule. Daniel saw that ‘judgment was given to the saints of the Most High’. The beast took their lives; Christ gives them life and a kingdom.

“Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection. Over these, the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him one thousand years” (v. 6). Whatever ‘the first resurrection’ means precisely, its promise is certain: those who belong to Christ will never face the second death. Jesus said, “he who hears my word, and believes him who sent me, has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life” (John 5:24).

sections.heading: The Last Rebellion
paragraphs: After the thousand years, “Satan will be released from his prison, and he will come out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog” (vv. 7–8). The names come from Ezekiel 38–39, where Gog leads a vast coalition against God's restored people. Here they stand for all the nations in a final rebellion. They surround “the camp of the saints, and the beloved city” (v. 9) — God's people, still a pilgrim camp.

There is no battle. “Fire came down out of heaven from God and devoured them” (v. 9). And “The devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet are also” (v. 10). The deceiver of Eden, the accuser of the brothers, the dragon of chapter 12 is finally and permanently defeated. Paul's promise is fulfilled: “And the God of peace will quickly crush Satan under your feet” (Romans 16:20).

Why would God release Satan at all? The text does not say, except that ‘he must’ (v. 3). Perhaps it shows that the human heart, even after the greatest blessings, still needs grace; and that God's final judgement falls on rebellion that is fully deliberate.

sections.heading: The Great White Throne
paragraphs: Then comes the final judgement. “I saw a great white throne, and him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away. There was found no place for them” (v. 11). There is nowhere left to hide. “I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life” (v. 12). Paul says, “For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ” (2 Corinthians 5:10).

There are two kinds of books. The ‘books’ record what each person has done: “The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works” (v. 12). God's judgement is fair; nothing is overlooked, and no one is judged for what they did not do. But there is also ‘the book of life’, the Lamb's register of those who belong to Him (13:8; 21:27). Salvation does not come from the record of works, which condemns us all, but from having one's name written in the book of life by grace. Those whose names are there are judged too — but their works are the fruit of faith, and their sins are covered by the Lamb's blood.

Everyone is raised: “The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them” (v. 13). Then “Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death” (v. 14). Paul wrote, “The last enemy that will be abolished is death” (1 Corinthians 15:26). And the chapter ends with the most sobering sentence in the book: “If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire” (v. 15). The only question that finally matters is whether your name is written there.

ntConnection.heading: Resurrection and Judgement
paragraphs: Jesus taught a resurrection of all: “the hour comes, in which all that are in the tombs will hear his voice, and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment” (John 5:28–29). He also spoke of a present, spiritual resurrection: “the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice; and those who hear will live” (John 5:25).

Paul described the order of resurrection: “But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then those who are Christ’s, at his coming. Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God” (1 Corinthians 15:23–24), and “For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy that will be abolished is death” (1 Corinthians 15:25–26).

He also said believers are already raised with Christ: God “raised us up with him, and made us to sit with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (Ephesians 2:6) — one reason some Christians see the reign of verse 4 as beginning now.

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “a thousand.” χίλιοι is the ordinary Greek number. The phrase ‘a thousand years’ (χίλια ἔτη), with ἔτος from the time family, gives us the word ‘millennium’ (Latin mille, thousand). Revelation uses numbers symbolically again and again (seven, twelve, 144,000, 666), and 1,000 is 10 × 10 × 10, a number of fullness. Whether the thousand years is a literal or symbolic period, it stands in contrast to the ‘short time’ given to Satan: Christ's reign is long and complete; Satan's freedom is brief.

Strong's: “a standing up again, i.e. (literally) a resurrection from death (individual, genitive case or by implication, (its author)), or (figuratively) a (moral) recovery (of spiritual truth).” ἀνάστασις, from the rise family, is literally ‘standing up again’. Strong's notes both a literal and a figurative sense — which is exactly why Christians differ over ‘the first resurrection’: is it bodily resurrection at Christ's return, or the believer's new life in Christ that death cannot end? Either way, those who share in it are blessed, holy and safe from the second death.

Strong's: “a fetter or manacle.” ἅλυσις was used of the chains that bound prisoners — Peter in prison (Acts 12:6–7), Paul ‘an ambassador in chains’ (Ephesians 6:20), and the demon-possessed man who broke his chains (Mark 5:3–4). Satan, who has chained so many, is himself chained. The apostles' chains could not stop the gospel; Satan's chain stops him from deceiving the nations.

Strong's: “to chop off (the head), i.e. truncate.” πελεκίζω, from πέλεκυς (an axe), refers to execution by beheading, the Roman punishment for citizens and the death of John the Baptist and, by tradition, of Paul. Those who refused the beast's image paid with their heads; they now receive thrones. Jesus said, ‘Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.’

Strong's: “Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist.” In Ezekiel 38–39, Gog is the ruler of the land of Magog, who leads a vast alliance of nations from the far north against God's people and is destroyed by fire from heaven. In Revelation ‘Gog and Magog’ are not a ruler and his land but the nations themselves, ‘in the four corners of the earth’. Even Strong's calls the name ‘symbolic’: the last great coalition of the world against God.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit shows you the end of Satan, death and judgement — and the only safe place to stand.

items.title: Satan Is on a Chain
items.body: A single angel binds the devil (v. 2). The Spirit wants you to stop fearing the enemy as if he were God's equal. He is a defeated foe on a chain, and his end is the lake of fire. Resist him; he must flee.

items.title: Faithfulness Is Rewarded
items.body: Those who were beheaded for Jesus now reign with Him (v. 4). The Spirit wants you to know that no sacrifice for Christ is wasted. What the world takes from you for His sake, He will repay with life and a throne.

items.title: Is Your Name in the Book?
items.body: “If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire” (v. 15). The Spirit asks the most important question there is: is your name written in the Lamb's book of life? If you are not sure, come to Jesus today. If you are, tell someone else.

audit.title: The Book of Life Check
audit.body: On what basis do you believe your name is written in the book of life — your works, or the Lamb's grace (vv. 12, 15)?

audit.title: The Accountability Check
audit.body: If the books of your life were opened today, what would you want to change (v. 12)?

audit.title: The Fear Check
audit.body: Do you live in fear of death? How does the destruction of Death and Hades (v. 14) change that?

practices.title: Settle the Question
practices.body: Read John 5:24 and Revelation 20:15 together. If you have never trusted Christ, pray now and ask Him to write your name in the book of life. If you have, write a prayer of thanks — and pray for three people by name whose names you long to see there.

practices.title: Live for the Throne
practices.body: Write down one costly act of faithfulness Christ is asking of you — forgiving, speaking up, giving, refusing a compromise. Do it this week, remembering that those faithful to death reign with Him (v. 4).

prayerReflection: “Lord God, You sit on the great white throne, and earth and heaven flee from Your face. Thank You that Satan is not Your equal, that a single angel can bind him, and that his end is the lake of fire. Thank You that those who were faithful to death, refusing the beast, now live and reign with Christ. Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection. Thank You that the second death has no power over those who belong to You. Lord Jesus, thank You that my name is written in Your book of life — not because of my works, but because of Your blood. When the books are opened, let my works be the fruit of Your grace. Thank You that You will throw Death and Hades into the fire, and that death will never touch Your people again. Help me live today in the light of that day, and give me a burden for those whose names are not yet written. Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Gog and Magog
storyConnections.summary: Ezekiel prophesied that after Israel's restoration, Gog of the land of Magog would gather a vast army from many nations and come against God's people ‘like a storm’. But God would rain down fire and brimstone, and Gog's army would fall on the mountains of Israel. Then all the nations would know that God is the LORD. Revelation 20 uses these names for the final rebellion of the nations — and the same fire from heaven ends it.

storyConnections.title: Daniel's Vision of Judgement
storyConnections.summary: Daniel saw thrones set in place and the Ancient of Days take His seat; His throne was fiery flames, and thousands upon thousands stood before Him. ‘The judgment was set, and the books were opened.’ The beast was slain, and ‘judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.’ Revelation 20 brings together both parts of Daniel's vision: thrones and judgement given to the saints, and the books opened before the great white throne.

storyConnections.title: The Strong Man Bound
storyConnections.summary: When the scribes accused Jesus of casting out demons by Beelzebul, He answered that Satan cannot cast out Satan. ‘But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.’ Jesus' casting out of demons showed that He had come to bind Satan and set his captives free. Revelation 20 pictures the same binding of the strong man, so that the nations can no longer be held in his deception.
